author: AfricanFeminism
title: Eight Years in Prison for Fighting Anti-Black Racism in Tunisia: Free Saadia Mosbah!
content:
For years, Saadia Mosbah has been one of the leading voices against anti-Black racism in Tunisia. As president of the anti-racism organisation Mnemty, she has stood up for Black Tunisians and Black migrants alike. When

 

violence against Black migrants escalated

 after President Kais Saied’s February 2023 statement against African migrants, she became a target of online hate campaigns.




On May 6, 2024, she was arrested. On March 19, 2026, she was sentenced to eight years in prison and a heavy fine on charges of money laundering and illicit enrichment. On June 23, the Tunis Court of Appeals upheld her conviction, along with those of five Mnemty colleagues and associates. A final appeal, filed on June 29, is now before the Court of Cassation.




Human rights movements and organisations,

 

including Amnesty International

, have denounced the irregularities in the proceedings and the lack of evidence for the alleged offences. They have also raised the alarm over the racist treatment and violence Saadia has reportedly suffered in detention.




Saadia’s case sits within a wider pattern of repression. Since President Kais Saied seized sweeping powers in July 2021, Tunisia has slid back into authoritarian rule. Since May 2024, the month of Saadia’s arrest, the authorities have waged 

a systematic crackdown on civil society
